findings.description: The RDS instance sets storage_encrypted = false, so the database volume and its snapshots hold data in cleartext, exposing sensitive application data if the underlying storage or a snapshot is accessed or shared.

publicly_accessible = true gives the MySQL instance a public endpoint reachable from the internet, so the VPC-scoped ingress rule is the only barrier and the database attack surface is greatly enlarged.

The master username is the predictable default 'admin' and the password comes from a plain Terraform variable (no Secrets Manager/KMS backing), so it is persisted in cleartext in Terraform state and reused verbatim in EC2 user data; combined with the public endpoint this is a direct credential-exposure and brute-force path.

The MySQL parameter group sets only character-set parameters and does not set require_secure_transport = 1, so the publicly accessible database accepts unencrypted client connections and credentials/data can traverse the network in cleartext.

The user_data script interpolates the RDS master username and var.password into a PHP include file; user data is stored unencrypted and retrievable from the instance metadata service (e.g. via SSRF in the deployed PHP app) and readable through the EC2 API/console.

No metadata_options block enforcing http_tokens = "required" is present, leaving IMDSv1 enabled; an SSRF in the hosted PHP application could retrieve the instance profile credentials for the highly privileged role and the plaintext DB password from user data.
No root_block_device with encrypted = true is specified, so the volume containing /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc with the database password may be stored unencrypted at rest.

The inline policy grants s3:*, ec2:* and rds:* on Resource "*" to the role attached to the web instance; theft of the instance profile credentials yields account-wide control of storage, compute and databases, including privilege-escalation paths via ec2:RunInstances and snapshot exfiltration.

Egress permits all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0 from the database security group, allowing unconstrained outbound data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised database tier.
